Reunion for director **[Adam Rehmeier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Carter_Rehmeier)** and star **Kyle Gallner**, who worked together on *[Dinner in America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinner_in_America)*.

title: The Root of the Game
capsule:
Brazilian deep dive doc series on the world of "várzea" — the passionate, precarious, and hugely popular amateur soccer scene in São Paulo's favelas.
Brazilian legends like **[Cafu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cafu)** and current stars like **[Raphinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raphinha)** appear, revisiting the humble beginnings that shaped their careers.

title: Love Is the Monster
capsule:
*[Midsommar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midsommar)*-inflected folk horror by way of a Finnish couples retreat (but shot in Canada).
**[Madeline Zima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeline_Zima)** of *Californication* and **[Leonardo Nam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Nam)** of *Westworld* fall into the hands of a cult trying to resurrect [Lempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lempo), the ancient Finnish goddess of love.

title: Love Is the Monster
capsule:
*[Midsommar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midsommar)*-inflected folk horror by way of a Finnish couples retreat (but shot in Canada).
**[Madeline Zima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madeline_Zima)** of *Californication* and **[Leonardo Nam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Nam)** of *Westworld* fall into the hands of a cult trying to resurrect [Lempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lempo), the ancient Finnish goddess of love.

title: A House Most Haunted
capsule:
Microbudget found footage horror.
The latest from indie horror regular **Kipp Tribble** (*The Stay*, *The Call*), who often writes, directs, and stars in his own shoestring productions.

title: Life of Mike
capsule:
Indie thriller about a real estate tycoon whose life implodes over the course of his birthday.
Feature debut from Atlanta-based black independent filmmaker **Derick Halliman**. **Halliman** also served as writer, producer, and cinematographer.

title: RADWIMPS 20th Anniversary Live Tour
capsule:
Concert film celebrating 20 years of the acclaimed Japanese rock band **[RADWIMPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radwimps)**.
Captures the final night of the tour at Tokyo's Ariake Arena.

title: Chapter 51
capsule:
Meta-Hollywood whodunit in the form of a true-crime documentary
Shot on literally every motion picture film format in existence—8mm, 16mm, 35mm, VistaVision, and 65mm IMAX—and using over 140 lenses.
From controversial photographer-turned-director **[Tyler Shields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Shields)**, who reteams with **[Abigail Breslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail_Breslin)** (*Little Miss Sunshine*, *Zombieland*) for the first time since his 2015 debut *Final Girl*.

title: We Are Pat
capsule: Trans and non-binary comedians join original creator **[Julia Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Sweeney)** to rewrite and reclaim one of *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live)*'s most controversial characters. Filmmaker **Rowan Haber** unpacks a childhood obsession, reframing a character once called "anti-trans propaganda" as a misunderstood, gender-defying icon. The film premiered at the 2025 Tribeca Festival, earning a Special Jury Mention. The infamous 1994 movie *[It's Pat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_Pat)* was based on a rejected first draft by **[Quentin Tarantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino)**.

title: Pardon Me: The Bevelyn B. Williams Story
capsule:
Biopic about the controversial pro-life activist **Bevelyn B. Williams**
stars model and reality-television personality **Angela White** (former-onlyfans-star-turned-christian **[Blac Chyna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blac_Chyna)**) in the lead role, a casting choice that aligns with her own publicly discussed turn to faith.
Also featuring MMA legend **[Quinton 'Rampage' Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampage_Jackson)**.

title: Vision Quest
capsule: Doc on four people on a challenging spiritual retreat in California's high desert.

title: Eagles of the Republic
capsule:
Political thriller about an Egyptian movie star pressured into starring in a state-sanctioned propaganda film.
The final installment of director **[Tarik Saleh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarik_Saleh)**'s "Cairo trilogy." Premiered in competition at the **[Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival)**.

title: Round the Decay
capsule:
New Hampshire folk horror.
The monster, a "Wrexsoul," was brought to life using practical effects. The film marks the return of **[Melody Kay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melody_Kay)** (*[The NeverEnding Story III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_NeverEnding_Story_III)*) to the screen after a 21-year hiatus from acting.

title: The Fun-Raiser
capsule:
Comedy about a last-ditch fundraiser for a performing arts school.
The fourth feature from Minneapolis-based director **Wyatt McDill**.

title: Hungry
capsule:
Killer hippo in the Louisiana bayou (but shot in Malta).
Loosely inspired by the *[Hungry Hungry Hippos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungry_Hungry_Hippos)* board game.
The film also taps into a bizarre-but-true piece of American history: a [1910 congressional plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hippo_bill) to import hippos into Louisiana's swamps to solve a meat shortage.

title: We Are Pat
capsule:
Trans filmmaker **Ro Haber** re-examines the 90s *[SNL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live)* character.
Joined by the character's creator, **[Julia Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Sweeney)**.
Premiered at the 2025 **[Tribeca Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Festival)**, where it received a Special Jury Mention for New Documentary Director.

title: Hold the Fort
capsule:
Horror-comedy "splat-stick" festival fav (Fantasia, Sitges, FrightFest)
Couple's move to the suburbs is interrupted when they learn their Homeowners Association's main job is fighting an annual onslaught of monsters from a portal to Hell.

title: The Clash of Nations: Joe Louis vs. Max Schmeling
capsule:
History Channel doc about the boxing rivalry that became a proxy war between America and Nazi Germany in the years leading up to WW2.
Executive produced by **[LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James)**.

title: Charlie Shaw's Revenge
capsule:
British killer clown flick.
Shot on location at the 65-acre Knockhatch Adventure Park and the East Sussex School of Circus Arts.

title: High Water
capsule:
British seaside noir.
Inspired by real-life murders that took place in Brighton.

title: Our Wolves: In a Landscape of Fear and Love
capsule:
Swiss doc on the fierce debate whether the return of wolves to the Italian Alps.
Director **Samer Angelone** is a biologist-turned-filmmaker, and his subject, professor **Luca Rossi**, was his former doctoral supervisor.
Won eight international awards, including Best Film at Australia’s [SCINEMA Science Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scinema).

title: The Sheep Detectives
capsule:
After a shepherd (**[Hugh Jackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Jackman)**) is mysteriously killed, his flock of sheep (voiced by the likes of **[Julia Louis-Dreyfus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Louis-Dreyfus)** and **[Bryan Cranston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Cranston)**) set out to solve the crime.
Writer **[Craig Mazin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Mazin)** (*Chernobyl*, *The Last of Us*) spent nearly a decade securing the rights to the German novel *Three Bags Full*.
First live-action movie by **[Kyle Balda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_Balda)** (director of *Minions* and *Despicable Me*).

title: In the Hand of Dante
capsule:
Passion project from painter-director **[Julian Schnabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Schnabel)** (*The Diving Bell and the Butterfly*).
Crime thriller about a stolen manuscript of Dante's *Divine Comedy*, intertwined with the story of Dante himself writing the masterpiece.
Incredible ensemble — **[Oscar Isaac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Isaac)** in a dual role, **[Gal Gadot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gal_Gadot)**, **[Gerard Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Butler)**, **Jason Momoa**, **Al Pacino**, and **Martin Scorsese** in a rare acting appearance.

title: Not So Perfect Stranger
capsule:
Made-for-TV stalker flick.
An architect with PTSD returns to her honeymoon spot in Niagara Falls, only to become the target of a disturbed local.
Lifetime

title: The Welcome Table
capsule:
Climate doc by **[Josh Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Fox)** (Oscar-nominated for *[Gasland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasland)*). Fox gathers disaster refugees from six continents (droughts in Kenya, floods in Bangladesh) and brings them to a 1,000-foot table on the New Orleans levee.
Local jazz musicians led by **[John Boutté](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Boutt%C3%A9)** play alongside the refugees' testimony. Also **[John Cameron Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cameron_Mitchell)**.
HBO Documentary Films.

title: Blast
capsule:
Action-paced Tamil-language kung fu flick.
A family of karate-chopping heroes is targeted by a ruthless corporate syndicate.

title: Unwelcomed
capsule:
Chilean documentary capturing the violent 2021 protests against Venezuelan immigrants.
The title, *Si Vas Para Chile*, ironically comes from a folk song that romantically welcomes foreigners.
World premiere at [Hot Docs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Docs).

title: The Reality Experiment
capsule:
Super low-budget Australian sci-fi. Eight strangers sign up for a quick payday in a university experiment, only to find reality itself unravelling.
Shot entirely in Sydney over a compressed schedule of roughly ten short shooting days across three months. The cast performed all their own stunts.
A January 2026 teaser quotes [Marcus Aurelius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Aurelius) ("Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth") and hints at a prototype device that can "bend your own reality to your will."

title: Little Brother
capsule:
Odd couple slob vs. square comedy with chaotic **[Eric André](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Andr%C3%A9)** loosening up an uptight **[John Cena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cena)**.
From the director of *[Ingrid Goes West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingrid_Goes_West)*.
The deep-bench cast includes **[Michelle Monaghan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Monaghan)**, **[Christopher Meloni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Meloni)** (*Law & Order: Organized Crime*), **[Sherry Cola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherry_Cola)** (*Joy Ride*), and **[Ego Nwodim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ego_Nwodim)** (*SNL*).

title: Why We Dream
capsule:
Doc about 100-year-old WWII vets visiting Normandy on the anniversary of D-Day.
Produced by Delta Airlines (yes). Part of their program of flying veterans back to France.
Directed by **Meredith Danluck**, who created tour visuals for **[Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9)** and **[Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z)**, and score by **[Hans Zimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Zimmer)**.
Premiered at Tribeca.

title: The Mission
capsule:
Uncensored, on-the-ground doc, secretly filmed inside Gaza's hospitals.
British trauma surgeon **Dr. Mohammed Tahir** volunteers in overwhelmed operating rooms during the bombardment of late 2024.
Directed by **The Gaza Collective**, a group working from within the conflict zone.

title: Chris & Martina: The Final Set
capsule:
Portrait of tennis legends **[Chris Evert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Evert)** and **[Martina Navratilova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martina_Navratilova)**, focusing on their decades-long 80-match rivalry. Off-court they became close friends when they both were diagnosed with and battled the same type of cancer.
From Emmy-winning director **Rebecca Gitlitz**, this Netflix documentary premiered at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival.

title: Savage House
capsule:
A black comedy set during the Jacobite uprising of 1715, with **[Richard E. Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_E._Grant)** (*Withnail & I*) and **[Claire Foy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claire_Foy)** (*The Crown*).
A lavish party goes horribly wrong, in this romp full of ruthless social climbing and decadent, bloody chaos, all set during a raging smallpox outbreak.
Critics compared its vicious wit to *The Favourite* and its cool irony to *Barry Lyndon*.

title: Strung
capsule:
Blumhouse made a **[Tyler Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Perry)** movie. **[Chlöe Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloe_Bailey)** stars as a violinist whose tutoring job for an elite family becomes a fight for her safety and sanity.
Director **[Malcolm D. Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_D._Lee)** usually makes comedies like *Girls Trip* and *The Best Man*.
Filmed in Cape Town, South Africa.

title: Above the Line
capsule:
Indie heist-comedy about six wannabe movie folks who team up to rob the Academy Awards.
Pitched as *Swingers* meets *Pulp Fiction*. Features **[Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer)**.

title: Summerween
capsule:
Killer clown slasher from The Asylum, the studio responsible for *Sharknado*.
First slasher built around "Summerween," a fake holiday celebrating Halloween during the summer, popularized by the animated series *Gravity Falls*.

title: Magic Hour
capsule:
**[Katie Aselton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katie_Aselton)** (*The League*) co-wrote this indie relationship drama with her husband **[Mark Duplass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Duplass)**.
She stars with **[Daveed Diggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveed_Diggs)** (*Hamilton*) as a couple escaping to the desert to do relationship stuff.
Premiered at SXSW, unsurprisingly.

title: Two Strangers Trying Not to Kill Each Other
capsule:
Intimate portrait of the 30-year marriage between world-renowned photographer **[Joel Meyerowitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Meyerowitz)** and his wife, artist and writer **Maggie Barrett**.
From Final Cut for Real, the six-time Oscar-nominated Danish production company behind *[Flee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flee_%28film%29)* and *[The Act of Killing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Act_of_Killing)*.

title: Carissa
capsule:
South African coming-of-age story that drew raves at the Venice Film Festival. Set in the Cederberg mountains, a young woman confronts the development of her grandfather's tea lands.
Feature debut from directors **Jason Jacobs** and **Devon Delmar**.

title: The American Experiment
capsule:
A five-part Netflix docuseries re-examining the founding of the United States.
Featuring interviews with **Kamala Harris**, **Mike Pence**, **Al Gore**, **Hillary Clinton**, and **Ted Cruz**, among others. **[Martin Sheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Sheen)** voices George Washington. Executive produced by **Tom Hanks**.

title: Tuner
capsule:
"a fun cool thriller jazzy heist movie… about a piano tuner", by **[Daniel Roher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Roher)**, winner of Best Doc Oscar for *Navalny*.
**[Leo Woodall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_Woodall)** (*White Lotus*) is a tuner with a hearing condition that gives him a unique aptitude for cracking safes. Nice supporting part by **[Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman)**.
Premiered at Telluride.

title: Power Ballad
capsule:
From the creator of *ONCE*, another modern musical: **[Paul Rudd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Rudd)** as a Dublin wedding singer vs. **[Nick Jonas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Jonas)** as a fading boy-band star, in this musical comedy.
Rudd does his own singing, covering Thin Lizzy's "The Boys Are Back in Town" and Bryan Adams' "Summer of '69."

title: Enola Holmes 3
capsule:
Third Enola Holmes movie, **[Millie Bobby Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Bobby_Brown)**'s hit series about the sister of Sherlock Holmes (**[Henry Cavill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cavill)**). This one's darker, a thriller by **[Philip Barantini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Barantini)**.
Filmed in Malta.

title: 40 Dates and 40 Nights
capsule:
High concept rom-com. A young woman who accepts her grandmother's (**[Annie Potts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Potts)**) challenge: 40 dates in 40 nights to win a full year of rent. Romance and comedy ensue.
Featuring **[Bailee Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailee_Madison)** (*Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin*) and **[Joel Courtney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Courtney)** (*The Kissing Booth*).

title: 40 Dates and 40 Nights
capsule:
High concept rom-com. A young woman who accepts her grandmother's (**[Annie Potts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Potts)**) challenge: 40 dates in 40 nights to win a full year of rent. Romance and comedy ensue.
Featuring **[Bailee Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailee_Madison)** (*Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin*) and **[Joel Courtney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Courtney)** (*The Kissing Booth*).

title: Carmeni Selvam
capsule:
Tamil comedy about a man whose life unravels when he gets a case of "money fever."
Stars two of Tamil cinema's most acclaimed directors in acting roles: **[P. Samuthirakani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._Samuthirakani)** (*Visaranai*) and **[Gautham Vasudev Menon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gautham_Vasudev_Menon)** (*Vaaranam Aayiram*)

title: The Memory Keeper
capsule: Canadian dystopian sci-fi—a future where memories have become government-regulated products. *Black Mirror*-esque.

title: In Symbiosis
capsule:
Exposé of the industrial food system (colonialism, climate crisis).
Eight-year, self-funded "labour of love".
Premiered at London's Raindance Film Festival.

title: Dom
capsule: Bosnian-Italian documentary following a woman's return to the Sarajevo orphanage she fled during the war.

title: Raja Shivaji
capsule:
Action epic about [Shivaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shivaji), the founder of India's [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire).
Decade-long passion project for director **[Deshmukh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riteish_Deshmukh)**, who also stars as the title role.

title: Louis C.K.: Ridiculous
capsule: **[Louis C.K.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_C.K.)** returns to Netflix. Filmed at the Beacon Theatre in New York City.

title: Fish Bone
capsule:
Coming-of-age drama: a young woman whose summer after high school goes sideways.
Premiered at the [Shanghai International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_International_Film_Festival); won Best Screenplay in the Asian New Talent section.

title: Yohanna
capsule:
Indonesian social-realism. A young nun gets pulled into the dangerous underworld of child labor.
The director cast local children with no acting experience, spending six months on the island just getting them comfortable with the camera.

title: She's the He!
capsule:
Two high school friends pose as trans women to quell gay rumors, and one realizes they are trans.
Premiered to a standing ovation at SXSW.

title: I Was a Teenage Sex Pistol
capsule:
[Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Pistols) saga from the perspective of **[Glen Matlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Matlock)**, their original bassist and key songwriter (co-writing 10 of the 12 songs on *[Never Mind the Bollocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Mind_the_Bollocks,_Here%27s_the_Sex_Pistols)* before being pushed out of the band).
Based on his memoir. Who's-who of talking heads, including **[Debbie Harry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Harry)** and **[Clem Burke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clem_Burke)** of [Blondie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blondie_%28band%29).

title: A Crime Story
capsule: Crime-comedy with a murderer's row of character actors (**[Jeff Fahey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Fahey)**, **[William Forsythe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Forsythe_%28actor%29)**, **[Mark Pellegrino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Pellegrino)**). A group of motel misfits who stumble on a briefcase of drug money.

title: Broken Harmony
capsule:
Atlanta-based music drama: a recording artist trying to save her career by returning to her roots.
Stars singer-songwriter **Reette Thorns**, who gained national attention as a contestant on *American Idol*. Oklahoma-based director **LaRonn Marzett** worked on projects for BET and The Asylum.

title: Bang My Box: The Robin Byrd Story
capsule:
HBO doc on **[Robin Byrd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Byrd)**'s cult, sex-positive Public Access call-in show in NYC from 1977–1998.
Produced by **[Sarah Jessica Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jessica_Parker)**.

title: Shadows of Willow Cabin
capsule:
Slow-burn cabin horror. More a fraught two-handed gay drama than a supernatural ghost story.
The feature directing debut of **Joe Fria**, best known for voicing Slappy the Dummy in the *Goosebumps* audiobook series.

title: Declarations: Black Americans and the Revolutionary War
capsule:
PBS doc about Black Americans who fought in the [Revolutionary War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War). Part of the PBS 'America @ 250' slate, timed for the nation's 250th anniversary.
Filmmakers commissioned oil portraits of the documentary's subjects and used AI to animate them.

title: Original Sound
capsule:
Indie flick about a Queens beat maker (**[David Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lambert_%28actor%29)**) whose track gets stolen by a rising pop star (**[Laura Marano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Marano)**), forcing them into a tense collaboration.
Adapted from the 2019 Off-Broadway play.
Screen directing debut of Tony Award-winning stage actor **[Gregory Jbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Jbara)** (*[Billy Elliot the Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Elliot_the_Musical)*).

title: Maiin Haan
capsule: Punjabi horror film, reportedly based on a true story from 2007.

title: The Sinking of the Lisbon Maru
capsule:
Chinese doc (and box office hit) about a forgotten WWII tragedy: the sinking of the British POW ship by friendly fire, and the local Chinese fishermen who rescued hundreds of survivors.
Features the last two living survivors. China's entry for Best Documentary at the Academy Awards.

title: This Is Birmingham
capsule:
Gritty British crime thriller set in Birmingham's underworld.
Passion project from filmmaker **Kay S. Ubhi**, who writes, directs, produces, and also stars as the ambitious son stepping up to claim his territory.

title: The Theft of the Caravaggio
capsule:
A fictionalized take on a real event — the audacious 1984 theft of [Caravaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caravaggio)'s masterpiece, *[Saint Jerome Writing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Jerome_Writing_%28Caravaggio,_Valletta%29)*.
Shot on 35mm.

title: Jacked
capsule:
Retro slasher set in Summer of '87.
All-Canadian '87 soundtrack: Spoons, The Cooper Brothers, Haywire.

title: Silent Friend
capsule:
A ginkgo tree in a German botanical garden silently observes three separate human lives in 1908, 1972, and 2020.
Hong Kong cinema legend **[Tony Leung Chiu-wai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Leung_Chiu-wai)** (*[In the Mood for Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Mood_for_Love)*) stars in his first European production.
Every tree and plant in the film is listed in the end credits alongside the actors.

title: Letty Lynton
capsule:
Notorious pre-Code melodrama unseen for nearly 90 years; pulled from circulation in 1936 after a plagiarism lawsuit.
**[Joan Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Crawford)** as a socialite who gets away with poisoning her obsessive former lover.
The white organdy gown with enormous ruffled sleeves designed by [Adrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrian_%28costume_designer%29) became a fashion sensation, with Macy's reportedly selling over 50,000 copies.

title: Animals in War
capsule:
Ukrainian war anthology film — seven true vignettes on the invasion told through the eyes of animals.
**[Sean Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Penn)** is in one segment.

title: A Super Progressive Movie
capsule:
Animated anti-LGBTQ+ political satire from Australian far-right leader [Pauline Hanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_Hanson) and her One Nation party.
Feature-length version of their web series *Pauline Hanson's Please Explain*.

title: Sun Ra: Do the Impossible
capsule:
Kaleidoscopic portrait of the visionary jazz musician, father of [Afrofuturism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrofuturism), philosopher, and poet **[Sun Ra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Ra)**.
From American Masters Pictures, the film arm of the legendary PBS documentary series *[American Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Masters)*.

title: Single Black Tenant
capsule:
Paranoid apartment-from-hell thriller starring **[Tia Mowry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tia_Mowry)** (*Sister, Sister*, *The Game*).
A Lifetime "Ripped from the Headlines" movie.

title: Super Happy Forever
capsule:
Japanese drama that swept the festival circuit, winning top prizes at [Film Fest Gent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_Fest_Gent) and the [Reykjavík International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reykjav%C3%ADk_International_Film_Festival) after premiering in [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival).
A man returns to the seaside town where he met and fell in love with his late wife.

title: Paid in Blood
capsule:
Brazilian documentary thriller centered on the 2017 [Pau D'Arco massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pau_D%27Arco_Massacre), where police killed ten landless workers in the Amazon.
Journalist-turned-director **Ana Aranha** arrived on the scene hours after the killings, and tracked the case for seven years.

title: Birthright
capsule: Australian black comedy about moving back home with your parents. Tribeca premiere, shot in Perth.

title: Rise of the Underdog
capsule:
True-story about a man trying to break into the film industry after a wrongful imprisonment. **Mack Lindon** wrote, directed, and starred as himself.
Follow-up of sorts to *[Rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rise_%282014_film%29)*, Lindon's 2014 debut dramatizing the same ordeal.

title: Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness: An almost History of America
capsule:
Sketch comedy series from **[Larry David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_David)**, improvising on major events in American history with friends from **[Bill Hader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Hader)** as Abraham Lincoln to **[Jurnee Smollett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurnee_Smollett)** as Rosa Parks.
Produced by **[Barack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)** and **[Michelle Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)**. Obama pitched it to Larry himself.

title: The Ark
capsule:
Ukrainian verité documentary about a couple who refuse to flee the Russian invasion—and instead turn their home into an improbable sanctuary for over 1,000 displaced animals.
Narrated and executive produced by **[Kyra Sedgwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyra_Sedgwick)** (*The Closer*), the film premiered at the 2025 Woodstock Film Festival.

title: Fiume o Morte!
capsule:
Experimental and comic doc about Italian poet and proto-fascist **[Gabriele D'Annunzio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriele_D%27Annunzio)**, who occupied the city of Fiume after World War I.
Director **Igor Bezinović** stages comic reenactments of this strange precursor to [Mussolini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benito_Mussolini)'s fascism.
Winner of the Tiger Award and the FIPRESCI prize at the [International Film Festival Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Film_Festival_Rotterdam).

title: Away with Words
capsule:
A brand-new silent movie in which actual silent-era stars — **[Louise Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Brooks)** and **[Wallace Beery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_Beery)** — appear alongside the living cast.
Writer-director **Samuel Pothier** stars as a title-card writer torn between the movie world in his head and a shot at real love.

title: The Last Guest of the Holloway Motel
capsule:
The quiet old man managing a shuttering West Hollywood motel — and its last resident — turns out to be **[Tony Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Powell_%28footballer%29)**, a soccer star who vanished without a trace forty years ago.
Found by the director in West Hollywood, who planned a 4-minute short about a closing motel but discovered far more.
One of Vogue's "5 Standout Films of [Tribeca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribeca_Festival) 2025."

title: The Broken R
capsule:
Intimate personal doc from **Ricardo Ruales Eguiguren**, a gay director with [Treacher Collins syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treacher_Collins_syndrome) (face-disfiguring).
The title refers to his inability to pronounce the letter "r".
A festival favorite, it had its world premiere at Sheffield Doc/Fest and also played at IDFA.

title: Paul Simon: The Quiet Celebration Concert
capsule:
Concert film capturing **[Paul Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Simon)**'s first-ever live performance of his Grammy-nominated album *[Seven Psalms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Psalms)*.
*Seven Psalms* is a meditative, seven-movement work performed in its entirety, as a single 33-minute acoustic piece (followed by newly arranged classics and deep cuts).
The tour marked Simon's return to the stage after overcoming significant hearing loss.

title: Corina
capsule:
[*Amélie*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%A9lie)-like quirky Mexican dramedy about a young woman with agoraphobia.
A festival favorite, winning audience awards at [SXSW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest) and top honors at the [Guadalajara Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara_International_Film_Festival).
Directed by [Diego Luna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Luna)'s former editor.

title: Notes from the Last Row
capsule:
Disillusioned literature professor (**[Choi Min-sik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choi_Min-sik)** from *Oldboy*) gets dangerously drawn into the stories of a quiet student in the back row.
Adapted from the celebrated Spanish play *El chico de la última fila* (also the basis for **[François Ozon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Ozon)**'s 2012 film *[In the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_House_%28film%29)*).

title: Away with Words
capsule:
**Samuel Pothier** stars opposite digitally resurrected legends of the original silent era like **[Louise Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Brooks)** and **[Wallace Beery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallace_Beery)**.
A reclusive title-card writer for silents in 1929 must choose between the world in his head and a chance at real love.

title: Escape
capsule:
Man believes the only solution to his problems is to live in jail, and will do whatever it takes to get there.
Director **[Rodrigo Cortés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrigo_Cort%C3%A9s)** (*[Buried](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buried_%28film%29)*) pitched it as "*[The Count of Monte Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Count_of_Monte_Cristo)* backwards."
Executive produced by **[Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese)**.

title: Molotov Cocktail
capsule:
70s-set Iranian comedy that unites some of the country's biggest stars — **Amin Hayaei**, **[Ahmad Mehranfar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Mehranfar)**, **Pejman Jamshidi**.
A down-on-his-luck man wins a lottery just as the 1979 revolution throws everything into chaos.

title: Inheritance
capsule: A personal essay-documentary: four bodies unearthed on the filmmaker's ancestral estate in Salamanca become the thread for excavating a family's — and a country's — buried Civil War past. Premiered at DocsBarcelona 2026.

title: Inheritance
capsule:
Eleven-years-in-the-making vérité documentary about a boy growing up in Appalachian Ohio inside a family shaped by addiction.
Directors **Matt Moyer** and **Amy Toensing** follow him from childhood,
Won the Slamdance 2024 Best Documentary Jury Award.

title: Painting With Fire
capsule: British artist **Tom de Freston** and blind Syrian academic **Ali Souleman** collaborate to translate Souleman's memories of war into paintings.

title: Isla Monstro
capsule:
Adult animated sci-fi comedy with an 80s creature-feature vibe. A loser washes ashore on a secret island overrun by mutant monsters and decides to turn it into a luxury resort.
Director **Steven Shea** taught himself animation from online tutorials, then animated the whole feature in his basement over a year.
The voice cast includes **[James Marsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Marsters)** (*Buffy the Vampire Slayer*), **[Spencer Grammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Grammer)** (*Rick and Morty*), **[John DiMaggio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_DiMaggio)** (*Futurama*), and comedian **[Harland Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harland_Williams)** (*Half Baked*).

title: American Youngboy
capsule:
**YoungBoy Never Broke Again** concert doc and profile, captured during his record-breaking "Make America Slime Again" tour. Audiences turning theatrical  screenings into viral, concert-like sing-alongs.

This 42-date, completely sold-out arena tour was a landmark event, grossing nearly $70 million and becoming the highest-grossing tour for a debut headlining rapper.

Directed by **Nico Ballesteros**, known for his years-long documentation of **Kanye West** for the film *In Whose Name?*.

title: The Story of Everything
capsule:
A cinematic argument for intelligent design-- backed by the Discovery Institute. 

 Traces evidence for a creator in cosmology, physics, and the spiral structure of DNA. Interviews with figures from the intelligent design movement alongside Silicon Valley entrepreneur **Peter Thiel**.

title: Night of the Living Dead
capsule:
Another direct-to-video remake of the 1969 zombie classic, George Romero--becaus the original is public domain due to a copyright error, there has been a pile of these remakes and unofficial sequels over the years.

From director **Christopher Ray**, known for his work with mockbuster studio The Asylum. Stars cult-favorite **[Robert Carradine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Carradine)** (*Revenge of the Nerds*).

title: Disney Celebrates America: The Pursuit of Happiness
capsule:
A primetime special using Disneyland (and other Disneyparks) as a portal to explore American history and traditions--timed to the 250th anniversary of the United States. 

Premiered on ABC on June 29, 2026--and the special was made available for streaming the following day on both Disney+ and Hulu.

title: The Last Whale Singer
capsule:
Environmentalist-themed children's film made by German-Iranian filmmaker over 15 years, mostly in Unreal Engine--- with plans for  a video game and a TV series.  T

Teenage humpback must find the mystical song that can save the oceans from a creature unleashed by a melting iceberg.

The Grand Jury Award for Best Animated Feature at the Blue Water Film Fest.

title: Living the Land
capsule:
Sprawling yet intimate portrait of a rural Chinese village in 1991, on the cusp of mass modernization. 

Cast of mostly non-professional actors,  hot over the course of a full year to authentically capture the changing seasons.

Director **Huo Meng**’s second feature won him the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2025 Berlin Film Festival.

title: Phantoms of July
capsule:
Deadpan German comedy that finds magical realism in a post-socialist landscape. A heartbroken waitress from East Germany and an Iranian YouTuber with a broken arm.

Director Julien Radmaier was hailed at its Locarno premiere as the "heir apparent to Peter Greenaway". He worked as an assistant to the legendary New German Cinema director Werner Schroeter, and has translated the works of French philosopher Jacques Rancière.

title: The Woman with Three Husbands
capsule:
Polyamorous TV movie thriller in the Lifetime tradition--but with "brother husbands" instead of sister wives.

 A woman investigates her brother’s new wife and her two other husbands, suspecting one is a killer.

title: Man of War
capsule:
Hard-hitting action set in the early days of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Former US Special Forces vet must cross into the warzone to rescue his adopted daughter.

Director **[William Kaufman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kaufman_%28director%29)** (*The Channel*, *Jarhead 3: The Siege*) makes direct-to-video action that punches above its budget with  brutal, practical, and tactical thrills.
